cur:catacombs-good-shepherd-trapezophoro.summary: A shepherd in a short tunic and leggings carries a large ram across his shoulders and leans on a knotted staff. The statue served as the support of a marble table, and its sturdy, frontal figure shows the Good Shepherd entering the repertoire of Christian sculpture in the round.
facts: The museum label describes it as the base of a lost marble altar or table, with the legs and the lamb's muzzle remodelled; its provenance is unknown.
It is displayed near the celebrated Good Shepherd statue in the same museum.
cur:catacombs-good-shepherd-trapezophoro.notes: The ram-bearer was a familiar pagan figure; its Christian meaning here is inferred from its context in the Christian collections and is not certain.

cur:objects-coin-constantine-vii-romanos.summary: On the obverse a facing bust of Christ blesses and holds the Gospels; on the reverse Constantine VII, now sole senior emperor, and his son Romanos II hold a patriarchal cross between them. The serene Pantokrator of this issue, with a carefully modelled face, reflects the classicising taste of Constantine VII's court. The coin carried Christ's image throughout the empire and far beyond its borders.
facts: Constantine VII became sole ruler in 945 after the fall of the Lekapenoi and crowned his son Romanos II co-emperor; this issue belongs to their joint reign (945–959).
cur:objects-coin-constantine-vii-romanos.notes: The CNG description notes a scuff across Christ's face on this specimen.
